rows.name: mRemoteNG
rows.reason: MRemoteNG manages operator-side RDP/VNC/SSH connections. As the whole solution, it does not supply the central self-hosted server and target-to-server arrangement; undocumented features are not declared unsupported.

rows.name: SimpleHelp with its Remote Access Service
rows.reason: SimpleHelp documents self-hosted Windows remote access with target-service registration. Registration/session firewall requirements remain unestablished; homepage testimonials do not supply sufficient verification.

rows.name: MeshLab
rows.reason: Its functions process and edit 3D geometry; it provides no remote-desktop agent, central access relay or firewall-traversal mechanism for Windows PCs.

rows.name: UltraVNC with a self-hosted Repeater and reverse connections
rows.reason: UltraVNC Windows services connect outward through a self-hosted repeater without public inbound endpoints. Requires endpoint setup, reachable relay ports, unique IDs, encryption/authentication; IDs alone provide insufficient security.

rows.name: MeshCentral with Windows MeshAgents
rows.reason: Self-hosted server and target-initiated Windows agents match the architecture. Callback documentation does not settle every manual target-firewall exception; verify connectivity under existing policy.

rows.name: PcHelpWare in repeater mode
rows.reason: PcHelpWare repeater mode documents attended Windows access without target firewall configuration. Self-owned repeater deployment and newer-target compatibility remain unverified; listed Windows versions are old.

rows.name: MeshCentral
rows.reason: Self-hosted server and outward-connecting Windows agents provide browser remote desktop without per-PC inbound ports; inspected architecture is dated 2019, so it is later evidence.

rows.name: Remote Utilities with a self-hosted RU Server and Internet-ID connections
rows.reason: Self-hosted Internet-ID relay avoids target inbound ports. Outbound policy must already permit connection; otherwise no-individual-firewall-change remains unresolved. Server reachability requires setup.

rows.name: MeshCentral
rows.reason: MeshCentral documents Windows-agent callbacks to self-hosted server port 443, with separate server firewall setup. No decisive conflict; existing target policy permitting connections without individual changes remains unresolved.

rows.name: Bitvise SSH Client reverse forwarding with RDP or VNC
rows.reason: Bitvise reverse SSH forwarding connects central access to outward-connected Windows desktops. Requires tunnels, credentials, port mapping and local desktop service; RDP needs a capable Windows edition. No turnkey portal.

rows.name: Remote Utilities with self-hosted RU Server
rows.reason: Self-hosted Internet-ID relay avoids inbound forwarding for Windows Hosts. Configure each Host; allowed outbound traffic and server reachability remain necessary. Current licensing does not establish 2016 terms.

rows.name: mRemoteNG
rows.reason: It organizes existing RDP, VNC and SSH connections but supplies no documented central relay or outbound agent that resolves the per-PC inbound-firewall constraint.

rows.name: MeshLab
rows.reason: MeshLab processes and edits 3D triangular geometry, outside remote-access workflows. Name similarity to MeshCentral does not establish a connection.

rows.name: SimpleHelp
rows.reason: Windows remote access connects outward to a customer server without target inbound ports. Requires agents, commercial licensing, server maintenance and permitted outbound traffic; exact 2016 features unproven.
